units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
Have you said good-night to my wife?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Comes C.
Crushing letter in her hand .
Yes.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Where is she?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: She is very tired. She has gone to bed. She said she had a headache.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: I must go to her. You’ll excuse me?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Rising hurriedly .

Oh, no! It’s nothing serious. She’s only very tired, that is all. Besides, there are people still in the supper-room. She wants you to make her apologies to them. She said she didn’t wish to be disturbed.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Drops letter .
She asked me to tell you!
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Picks up letter .
You have dropped something.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Oh yes, thank you, that is mine.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Puts out her hand to take it .
Still looking at letter .
But it’s my wife’s handwriting, isn’t it?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Takes the letter quickly .
Yes, it’s—an address. Will you ask them to call my carriage, please?
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Certainly.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Goes L. and Exit .

Thanks! What can I do? What can I do? I feel a passion awakening within me that I never felt before. What can it mean? The daughter must not be like the mother—that would be terrible. How can I save her? How can I save my child? A moment may ruin a life. Who knows that better than I? Windermere must be got out of the house; that is absolutely necessary.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Goes L.
But how shall I do it? It must be done somehow. Ah!
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Enter LORD AUGUSTUS R.U.E. carrying bouquet .
Dear lady, I am in such suspense! May I not have an answer to my request?
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Lord Augustus, listen to me. You are to take Lord Windermere down to your club at once, and keep him there as long as possible. You understand?
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: But you said you wished me to keep early hours!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Nervously .
Do what I tell you. Do what I tell you.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: And my reward?
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Your reward? Your reward? Oh! ask me that to-morrow. But don’t let Windermere out of your sight to-night. If you do I will never forgive you. I will never speak to you again. I’ll have nothing to do with you. Remember you are to keep Windermere at your club, and don’t let him come back to-night.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Exit L.
Well, really, I might be her husband already. Positively I might.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Follows her in a bewildered manner .
Lord Darlington’s Rooms .
A large sofa is in front of fireplace R. At the back of the stage a curtain is drawn across the window .
Doors L. and R. Table R. with writing materials.
Table C. with syphons, glasses, and Tantalus frame .
Table L. with cigar and cigarette box.
Lamps lit .
Standing by the fireplace .

Why doesn’t he come? This waiting is horrible. He should be here. Why is he not here, to wake by passionate words some fire within me? I am cold—cold as a loveless thing. Arthur must have read my letter by this time. If he cared for me, he would have come after me, would have taken me back by force. But he doesn’t care. He’s entrammelled by this woman—fascinated by her—dominated by her. If a woman wants to hold a man, she has merely to appeal to what is worst in him. We make gods of men and they leave us. Others make brutes of them and they fawn and are faithful. How hideous life is! . . . Oh! it was mad of me to come here, horribly mad. And yet, which is the worst, I wonder, to be at the mercy of a man who loves one, or the wife of a man who in one’s own house dishonours one? What woman knows? What woman in the whole world? But will he love me always, this man to whom I am giving my life? What do I bring him? Lips that have lost the note of joy, eyes that are blinded by tears, chill hands and icy heart. I bring him nothing. I must go back—no; I can’t go back, my letter has put me in their power—Arthur would not take me back! That fatal letter! No! Lord Darlington leaves England to-morrow. I will go with him—I have no choice.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Sits down for a few moments .
Then starts up and puts on her cloak .

No, no! I will go back, let Arthur do with me what he pleases. I can’t wait here. It has been madness my coming. I must go at once. As for Lord Darlington—Oh! here he is! What shall I do? What can I say to him? Will he let me go away at all? I have heard that men are brutal, horrible . . . Oh!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Hides her face in her hands .
Enter MRS. ERLYNNE L.
Lady Windermere!
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: LADY WINDERMERE starts and looks up .
Then recoils in contempt .
